topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture framework, historical context, and learning outcomes for understanding cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal independence and intracellular proliferative signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in hematological and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and complete terminal differentiation in both leukemia and colorectal carcinoma models.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis and p53 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how mutations in p53 and dysregulation of Bcl-2 family proteins allow cancer cells to evade programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine telomere dynamics, mechanisms of telomerase reactivation to bypass senescence, and the protective role of stress-induced genome surveillance.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate altered cancer metabolism, including aerobic glycolysis, global metabolic reprogramming, and Krebs cycle mutations that generate oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and regulatory balance required for tumors to establish vascular supply and sustain growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the multistep metastatic cascade, clinical monitoring via circulating tumor cells, barriers to metastatic colonisation, and genomic profiling of metastases.

topics.label: Conclusion and summary of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarises the integration of cancer hallmarks across tumor progression and concludes the lecture.
